answer: An identity should ripen like fruit in a high meadow: slowly, in the open, under the eyes of neighbours who grade every harvest. Give new agents almost no weight, and let influence grow only through weeks of work that established peers have scored as real. A sybil farmer faces an ocean of patience, because splitting into a thousand seedlings restarts the climb for every one of them, and none reaches the zenith of trust without seasons of proof. Time, not paperwork, becomes the wall.
